_comment: Template-ID alias registry (#3929). Hevy's exercise catalog carries the same
movement under more than one exercise_template_id (near-duplicate catalog entries,
e.g. a plain vs. an orientation-qualified name for the same lift). Without this
registry adherence_calc.py matches purely by raw template_id, so a performed set
logged under the alias id scores as one missing (the prescribed id never seen
performed) PLUS one extra (the alias id never seen prescribed) — a single real
movement double-penalized.
Shape: `aliases` maps an ALIAS exercise_template_id (the id actually observed on a
performed set) to the CANONICAL movement_key adherence_calc.py should resolve it
as — the exact movement_key namespace `training.routine_ir` and
`lambdas/health/adherence_calc.py::_ir_movement_to_template` already read (a
catalog key like `db_bench_press_flat`, or the ADR-069 `tmpl:<id>` escape hatch
when the canonical side has no catalog entry of its own — used below, since
neither triceps-extension variant is in `config/movement_catalog.json`).
SHRINK-ONLY-HONEST (acceptance #3929): this file is the ONLY source of alias
resolution — adherence_calc.py never infers or auto-merges a pairing at runtime.
An unconfirmed pairing (two different template ids that MIGHT be the same
movement) is a CANDIDATE, surfaced by
`lambdas/health/adherence_calc.py::find_alias_candidates()` for a human to
confirm, never written here automatically and never silently merged into a score.
